newsitem.title: USA: Rhone-Poulenc Rorer expands Granocyte deal.
newsitem.headline: Rhone-Poulenc Rorer expands Granocyte deal.

text.p: Rhone-Poulenc Rorer Inc said Wednesday that it has acquired an exclusive license to market Granocyte (lenograstim) in 39 additional countries, giving it the right to market the drug in a total of 79 countries.
Granocyte is a genetically engineered drug that stimulates the production of specific white blood cells, called neutrophils, the body's natural defenders against infection.
The license was acquired from Chugai Pharmaceutical Co Ltd.

In 1990, RPR and Chugai Pharmaceuticals created the joint venture Chugai Rhone-Poulenc which has developed and registered Granocyte throughout Western Europe, where it is marketed by Rhone Rorer in 17 countries, with export rights to a further 23 countries, mainly in Africa.
Under the new agreement, Rhone Rorer will now have the right to market Granocyte in 39 additional countries in Eastern Europe, South America, the Middle East, Asia and Africa.
Rhone Rorer will pay Chugai a royalty based on sales, it said.
